result.text: Title: LAN Party You are planning a LAN party for 10 friends, so the first thing you have to do is to send invitations to these 10 friends.
Next, you have to find out which games they want to play.
As soon as you have received a list of games, you can appoint a date when the LAN party is going to happen.
If 8 or more people agree on this date, you are good to continue.
Else, you have to appoint another date, until 8 people are free to join you.
While you find a date, you can find out if you have all the games your guests want to play.
If some are missing, download them.
Next, you should find out how much beer your friends will require.
If you do not have enough, buy what's missing.
After that, you can enjoy the LAN party.

result.process_description:
Title: LAN Party

You are planning a LAN party for 10 friends, so the first thing you have to do is to send invitations to these 10 friends.
Next, you have to find out which games they want to play.
As soon as you have received a list of games, you can appoint a date when the LAN party is going to happen.
If 8 or more people agree on this date, you are good to continue.
Else, you have to appoint another date, until 8 people are free to join you.
While you find a date, you can find out if you have all the games your guests want to play.
If some are missing, download them.
Next, you should find out how much beer your friends will require.
If you do not have enough, buy what's missing.
After that, you can enjoy the LAN party.

result.rule: When the description states that a condition or decision leads to a distinct action before subsequent work: Model the action as a separate task on the corresponding branch, and connect it to the preceding and subsequent work as described, including any return flow.

When the description states that a condition starts a distinct phase and separately names activities included in that phase: Model the conditional branch to the phase-start activity or subprocess, then represent the included activities within that phase rather than using one of them as the branch target.

When the description explicitly orders activities or says that work continues until a stated condition is reached: Model the activities in the stated sequence, and do not represent them as parallel or mutually exclusive branches unless the description explicitly supports concurrency or a decision.

When the description distinguishes an action that occurs before a later recording, confirmation, or other outcome: Model that action as a distinct activity in the sequence; do not omit it or use a terminal outcome event as its substitute.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
